text: The largest island in the Caribbean, known for classic cars, cigars, and a 1959 revolution.
A South American country with some of the largest oil reserves in the world and the tallest uninterrupted waterfall, Angel Falls.
An East African country containing the source of the Nile at Lake Victoria.
An East African nation known for the Maasai Mara, long-distance runners, and a capital whose name means 'cool water'.
A Southeast Asian kingdom whose flag features the temple complex of Angkor Wat.
A landlocked Alpine country known for neutrality, banks, watches, and four national languages.
The largest country in South America, home to most of the Amazon rainforest and famous for its Carnival celebrations.
A landlocked Central Asian country with the Hindu Kush mountains, often called the graveyard of empires.
A South American country known for tango, Patagonia, and beef, with a capital on the Río de la Plata.
A landlocked South American country with the world's largest salt flat and two capital cities.
A small eastern Mediterranean country with a cedar tree on its flag.
A Scandinavian country with dramatic fjords, a long Atlantic coastline, and wealth from North Sea oil.
A small Nordic kingdom made up of a peninsula and many islands, home to Lego and a little mermaid statue.
A central European country whose capital was largely rebuilt after World War II, birthplace of Copernicus and Chopin.
A Middle Eastern kingdom home to the rock-carved city of Petra and part of the Dead Sea.
An East African country that was never colonized, with its own calendar and an ancient Christian tradition.
An East African country home to Mount Kilimanjaro, the Serengeti, and the island of Zanzibar.
A southern African country that shares Victoria Falls and is named after an ancient stone city.
The largest landlocked country in the world, home to a major space launch site in Baikonur.
A teardrop-shaped island south of India, famous for its tea and formerly known as Ceylon.
A Southeast Asian archipelago of over 7,000 islands that was a Spanish and later American colony.
An Iberian country known for flamenco, siestas, and the unfinished Sagrada Família basilica.
A secretive East Asian state on a peninsula, ruled by the same family dynasty since 1948.
A North African country mostly covered by desert, with a long Mediterranean coast and large oil reserves.
A landlocked South American country where Guaraní is an official language alongside Spanish.
The largest country in Africa by area, most of which is covered by the Sahara.
A Central American country famous for a canal that connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
A desert kingdom on the Arabian Peninsula that contains Islam's two holiest cities.
The westernmost country on the African mainland, with its capital Dakar on a peninsula.
A landlocked country between two giants of Asia, with vast steppes and a nomadic herding tradition.
A North American country known for Aztec and Maya ruins, Day of the Dead celebrations, and its capital built on a former lake.
A large island off southeast Africa where lemurs and most of its wildlife are found nowhere else on Earth.
A central European country whose capital is split by the Danube into two historic halves.
A Balkan country with a long Adriatic coastline and the walled city of Dubrovnik.
A federation of seven emirates on the Persian Gulf, home to the world's tallest building.
The most populous country in Africa, with a booming film industry nicknamed Nollywood.
A country occupying the eastern half of a large island, with more than 800 languages spoken.
A small European country that hosts the headquarters of the EU and is famous for waffles and chocolate.
A Caribbean nation that became the first independent Black republic after a successful slave revolt in 1804.
A Southeast Asian kingdom that was never colonized by Europeans, famous for its street food and Buddhist temples.
A densely populated South Asian country in the Ganges delta, known for the Sundarbans mangrove forest.
A southern European country of many islands, considered the birthplace of democracy and the Olympic Games.
A very long and narrow South American country stretching along the Pacific, containing the Atacama Desert.
The only South American country with coastlines on both the Pacific and the Caribbean, famous for coffee.
An East Asian country with a Great Wall, the world's largest high-speed rail network, and giant pandas.
The only landlocked country in Southeast Asia, with the Mekong River running along much of its border.
An island country in the North Atlantic known as the Emerald Isle, celebrating a patron saint every March 17.
A central European country whose capital is known as the City of a Hundred Spires and is famous for pilsner beer.
A boot-shaped peninsula in southern Europe that once was the center of a vast ancient empire.
A Himalayan country containing the world's highest mountain and a non-rectangular national flag.
A small Baltic country known as one of the world's most digital societies, offering e-residency.
A West African country that in 1957 became one of the first in sub-Saharan Africa to gain independence, formerly called the Gold Coast.
A North African country where the Nile flows north into the Mediterranean, known for ancient pyramids and pharaohs.
A low-lying European country famous for windmills, tulips, and an extensive system of dikes.
A country at the southern tip of a continent that has three capital cities and was led by Nelson Mandela.
An island country in the South Pacific, where the Māori people live and where a famous fantasy film trilogy was shot.
An Alpine country that was the heart of the Habsburg empire and the home of Mozart.
A Southeast Asian country split between a peninsula and part of the island of Borneo, with famous twin towers.
The westernmost country of mainland Europe, birthplace of fado music and navigator Vasco da Gama.
Part of a larger union, this northern country is known for kilts, bagpipes, whisky, and a lake monster legend.
A country straddling Europe and Asia, whose largest city was once called Constantinople.
The most populous country in the world as of the 2020s, with a parliamentary democracy and the Taj Mahal.
A Western European country famous for a wrought-iron tower, wine regions like Bordeaux, and a revolution in 1789.
A Southeast Asian country formerly called Burma, known for thousands of temples in Bagan.
A Central American country that abolished its army in 1948 and is known for biodiversity and eco-tourism.
The largest country in the world by area, spanning eleven time zones across Europe and Asia.
A South American country named after the line that passes through it, which also owns the Galápagos Islands.
A Caribbean island that gave the world reggae music and a record-breaking sprinter.
A small, hilly East African country known as the land of a thousand hills, home to mountain gorillas.
An island nation made up of four constituent countries, with a constitutional monarchy and a parliament in Westminster.
An island nation in East Asia known for cherry blossoms, bullet trains, and a capital that is one of the largest cities in the world.
The northernmost country in Africa, home to the ruins of Carthage.
An eastern European country known as a breadbasket, with a blue and yellow flag and its capital on the Dnieper River.
A southwestern African country with towering red sand dunes and the Skeleton Coast.
A Scandinavian country known for flat-pack furniture, a pop group from the 1970s, and the Nobel Prizes.
A large central African country that contains most of the Congo rainforest and huge mineral reserves.
A Middle Eastern country formerly known as Persia, home to the ancient ruins of Persepolis.
A Middle Eastern country between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, the heart of ancient Mesopotamia.
A Central American country with many volcanoes and the Maya ruins of Tikal.
A Central Asian country with the Silk Road cities of Samarkand and Bukhara.
An eastern European country whose region of Transylvania is linked to the Dracula legend.
The world's largest archipelagic country, with more than 17,000 islands including Java and Bali.
A small Middle Eastern country bordering the Mediterranean, with Tel Aviv as its main economic center.
A landlocked West African country home to the historic city of Timbuktu.
A South Pacific nation of over 300 islands, known for rugby and coral reefs.
A country that is also a continent, home to kangaroos, koalas, and a famous opera house on a harbor.
A Nordic country with tens of thousands of lakes, a love of saunas, and a language unrelated to its Scandinavian neighbors.
A small peninsular Gulf state that hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup.
A South American country where the ruins of Machu Picchu sit high in the Andes.
A tiny, wealthy city-state at the tip of the Malay Peninsula known for its strict laws and hawker centres.
A Caribbean country that shares the island of Hispaniola and is passionate about baseball.
A volcanic North Atlantic island with geysers, glaciers, and one of the oldest parliaments in the world.
A central European country reunified in 1990, known for its autobahns and Oktoberfest.
A long, narrow Southeast Asian country shaped like an S, known for Ha Long Bay and phở.
An East Asian country on a peninsula, famous for K-pop, kimchi, and major electronics companies.
A South Asian country created in 1947, home to K2 and the ancient city of Mohenjo-daro.
A landlocked southern African country containing the Okavango Delta and many elephants.
The second-largest country by area, it has two official languages and a maple leaf on its flag.
A North African kingdom with coastlines on both the Atlantic and the Mediterranean, known for the medinas of Fez and Marrakesh.
A small South American country between two giants that won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930.
